# Independent properties 

```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(DT)

# Read the data
df <- read_csv("~/7.Narration/0.Consolidate/Input/1.Independent/independent_properties_1749538128833.csv")

# 1. Highest Total Land Area
max_land_area <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm)
max_neighborhood <- max_land_area$NEIGHBORHOOD
max_area <- max_land_area$TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm

# 2. Highest Average Land Area per Property
top_avg_land <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
first_neighborhood <- top_avg_land$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
first_avg_area <- top_avg_land$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[1]
second_neighborhood <- top_avg_land$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
second_avg_area <- top_avg_land$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[2]

# 3. Most Properties
max_properties <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `No. of Properties`, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
prop_neighborhood <- max_properties$NEIGHBORHOOD
prop_count <- max_properties$`No. of Properties`
prop_avg_area <- max_properties$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`

# 4. Most Vacant Land
max_vacant <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`NO. OF VACANT LAND`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `NO. OF VACANT LAND`)
vacant_neighborhood <- max_vacant$NEIGHBORHOOD
vacant_count <- max_vacant$`NO. OF VACANT LAND`

# 5. Least Developed Area
least_properties <- df %>%
  slice(which.min(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `No. of Properties`, `NO. OF VACANT LAND`)
least_prop_neighborhood <- least_properties$NEIGHBORHOOD
least_prop_count <- least_properties$`No. of Properties`
least_vacant_count <- least_properties$`NO. OF VACANT LAND`

# 6. Compact Neighborhoods with Large Plots
compact_large_plots <- df %>%
  filter(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm < median(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
compact_neighborhood_1 <- compact_large_plots$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
compact_avg_area_1 <- compact_large_plots$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[1]
compact_neighborhood_2 <- compact_large_plots$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
compact_avg_area_2 <- compact_large_plots$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[2]

# 7. Smaller Neighborhood with High Plot Size
small_high_plot <- df %>%
  filter(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm < quantile(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, 0.25)) %>%
  slice(which.max(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
small_neighborhood <- small_high_plot$NEIGHBORHOOD
small_total_area <- small_high_plot$TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm
small_avg_area <- small_high_plot$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`

# 8. Mid-range Balanced Development
mid_range <- df %>%
  filter(between(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, quantile(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, 0.25), quantile(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, 0.75)),
         between(`No. of Properties`, quantile(`No. of Properties`, 0.25), quantile(`No. of Properties`, 0.75))) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
mid_neighborhood_1 <- mid_range$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
mid_neighborhood_2 <- mid_range$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]

# 9. Opportunity Zones
opportunity_zones <- df %>%
  filter(`NO. OF VACANT LAND` > median(`NO. OF VACANT LAND`),
         `No. of Properties` > median(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`NO. OF VACANT LAND`)) %>%
  slice(1:3) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
opp_zone_1 <- opportunity_zones$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
opp_zone_2 <- opportunity_zones$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
opp_zone_3 <- opportunity_zones$NEIGHBORHOOD[3 %in% seq_len(nrow(opportunity_zones))] %||% "None"
opp_zone_3 <- opp_zone_3[3]
# 10. Urban Planning Insight (uses variables from previous points)
high_density_zone <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
high_density_neighborhood <- high_density_zone$NEIGHBORHOOD
low_density_1 <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
low_density_neighborhood_1 <- low_density_1$NEIGHBORHOOD
low_density_2 <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
low_density_neighborhood_2 <- low_density_2$NEIGHBORHOOD

# Display the datatable
datatable(df)
```

### Report-1

1. Highest Total Land Area:   **`r max_neighborhood`** has the largest total land area at  **`r format(max_area, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`** sqm, significantly higher than other neighborhoods, indicating its dominance in spatial coverage.

2. 3. 4. Vacant Land Availability: **`r vacant_neighborhood`** also leads in the number of vacant lands (**`r format(vacant_count, big.mark = ",")`**), suggesting potential for further development or future real estate opportunities.

5. Least Developed Area: **`r least_prop_neighborhood`** has the fewest properties (**`r format(least_prop_count, big.mark = ",")`**) and only (**`r format(least_vacant_count, big.mark = ",")`**) vacant lands, implying it is either fully developed, highly exclusive, or underdeveloped.

6. Compact Neighborhoods with Large Plots: **`r compact_neighborhood_1`** and **`r compact_neighborhood_2`** both show high average land areas (**`r format(compact_avg_area_1, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`** sqm and **`r format(compact_avg_area_2, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`** sqm) despite having relatively small total land areas, suggesting spacious, low-density developments.

7. Smaller Neighborhood with High Plot Size: **`r small_neighborhood`** is notable for its small total land area (**`r format(small_total_area, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`** sqm) but a high average land size (**`r format(small_avg_area, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)`** sqm), indicating fewer but larger properties.

8. Mid-range Balanced Development: **`r mid_neighborhood_1`** and **`r mid_neighborhood_2`** fall into a middle ground, with balanced figures across land area, number of properties, and vacant plots, indicating stable, moderately dense development.

9. Opportunity Zones: **`r opp_zone_1`**, **`r opp_zone_2`**, and **`r opp_zone_3`** may offer the best opportunities for real estate development or investment due to their combination of high vacant land count and property numbers.

10. Urban Planning Insight: The data reflects a clear variation in urban planning, from high-density zones like **`r high_density_neighborhood`** to low-density luxury areas like **`r low_density_neighborhood_2`** and **`r low_density_neighborhood_1`**. This has implications for infrastructure, zoning, and investment strategies.

# Government Properties 

```{r,message=FALSE,warning=FALSE,echo=FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(DT)

# Read the data
df <- read_csv("~/7.Narration/0.Consolidate/Input/2.Government/governmental_properties_1749538166171.csv")

# 1. Highest Total Land Area
max_land_area <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm)
max_neighborhood <- max_land_area$NEIGHBORHOOD
max_area <- max_land_area$TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm

# 2. Highest Average Land Area per Property
top_avg_land <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
first_neighborhood <- top_avg_land$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
first_avg_area <- top_avg_land$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[1]
second_neighborhood <- top_avg_land$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
second_avg_area <- top_avg_land$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[2]

# 3. Most Properties
max_properties <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `No. of Properties`, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
prop_neighborhood <- max_properties$NEIGHBORHOOD
prop_count <- max_properties$`No. of Properties`
prop_avg_area <- max_properties$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`

# 4. Most Vacant Land
max_vacant <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`NO. OF VACANT LAND`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `NO. OF VACANT LAND`)
vacant_neighborhood <- max_vacant$NEIGHBORHOOD
vacant_count <- max_vacant$`NO. OF VACANT LAND`

# 5. Least Developed Area
least_properties <- df %>%
  slice(which.min(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `No. of Properties`, `NO. OF VACANT LAND`)
least_prop_neighborhood <- least_properties$NEIGHBORHOOD
least_prop_count <- least_properties$`No. of Properties`
least_vacant_count <- least_properties$`NO. OF VACANT LAND`

# 6. Compact Neighborhoods with Large Plots
compact_large_plots <- df %>%
  filter(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm < median(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
compact_neighborhood_1 <- compact_large_plots$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
compact_avg_area_1 <- compact_large_plots$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[1]
compact_neighborhood_2 <- compact_large_plots$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
compact_avg_area_2 <- compact_large_plots$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`[2]

# 7. Smaller Neighborhood with High Plot Size
small_high_plot <- df %>%
  filter(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm < quantile(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, 0.25)) %>%
  slice(which.max(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD, TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, `AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)
small_neighborhood <- small_high_plot$NEIGHBORHOOD
small_total_area <- small_high_plot$TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm
small_avg_area <- small_high_plot$`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`

# 8. Mid-range Balanced Development
mid_range <- df %>%
  filter(between(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, quantile(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, 0.25), quantile(TOTAL_LAND_AREA_sqm, 0.75)),
         between(`No. of Properties`, quantile(`No. of Properties`, 0.25), quantile(`No. of Properties`, 0.75))) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
mid_neighborhood_1 <- mid_range$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
mid_neighborhood_2 <- mid_range$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]

# 9. Opportunity Zones
opportunity_zones <- df %>%
  filter(`NO. OF VACANT LAND` > median(`NO. OF VACANT LAND`),
         `No. of Properties` > median(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`NO. OF VACANT LAND`)) %>%
  slice(1:3) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
opp_zone_1 <- opportunity_zones$NEIGHBORHOOD[1]
opp_zone_2 <- opportunity_zones$NEIGHBORHOOD[2]
opp_zone_3 <- opportunity_zones$NEIGHBORHOOD[3 %in% seq_len(nrow(opportunity_zones))] %||% "None"
opp_zone_3 <- opp_zone_3[3]
# 10. Urban Planning Insight (uses variables from previous points)
high_density_zone <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`No. of Properties`)) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
high_density_neighborhood <- high_density_zone$NEIGHBORHOOD
low_density_1 <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
low_density_neighborhood_1 <- low_density_1$NEIGHBORHOOD
low_density_2 <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA(sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(2) %>%
  select(NEIGHBORHOOD)
low_density_neighborhood_2 <- low_density_2$NEIGHBORHOOD

# Display the datatable
datatable(df)
```

# Projects

```{r,echo=FALSE,warning-FALSE}
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(DT)
library(openxlsx)
# Create the dataframe
df <- read.xlsx("~/7.Narration/0.Consolidate/Input/3.Projects/projects.xlsx")
colnames(df)[colnames(df)=="PROJECT.NAME"] <- "PROJECT NAME"
colnames(df)[colnames(df)=="TOTAL.LAND.AREA.(sqm)"] <- "TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)"
colnames(df)[colnames(df)=="AVG..LAND.AREA.(sqm)"] <- "AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)"
colnames(df)[colnames(df)=="NO..OF.PROPERTIES"] <- "NO. OF PROPERTIES"
colnames(df)[colnames(df)=="NO.OF.PLOTS"] <- "NO OF PLOTS"
# colnames(df)[colnames(df)=="PROJECT.NAME"] <- "PROJECT NAME"

# 1. Highest Total Land Area
max_land_area <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`)
max_project <- max_land_area$`PROJECT NAME`
max_area <- max_land_area$`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`

# 2. Highest Average Land Area per Property
top_avg_land <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)
first_project <- top_avg_land$`PROJECT NAME`[1]
first_avg_area <- top_avg_land$`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`[1]
second_project <- top_avg_land$`PROJECT NAME`[2]
second_avg_area <- top_avg_land$`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`[2]

# 3. Most Properties
max_properties <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`)) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `NO. OF PROPERTIES`, `AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)
prop_project <- max_properties$`PROJECT NAME`
prop_count <- max_properties$`NO. OF PROPERTIES`
prop_avg_area <- max_properties$`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`

# 4. Most Vacant Plots
max_vacant <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`NO OF PLOTS`)) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `NO OF PLOTS`)
vacant_project <- max_vacant$`PROJECT NAME`
vacant_count <- max_vacant$`NO OF PLOTS`

# 5. Least Developed Area
least_properties <- df %>%
  slice(which.min(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`)) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `NO. OF PROPERTIES`, `NO OF PLOTS`)
least_prop_project <- least_properties$`PROJECT NAME`
least_prop_count <- least_properties$`NO. OF PROPERTIES`
least_vacant_count <- least_properties$`NO OF PLOTS`

# 6. Compact Projects with Large Plots
compact_large_plots <- df %>%
  filter(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)` < median(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)
compact_project_1 <- compact_large_plots$`PROJECT NAME`[1]
compact_avg_area_1 <- compact_large_plots$`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`[1]
compact_project_2 <- compact_large_plots$`PROJECT NAME`[2]
compact_avg_area_2 <- compact_large_plots$`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`[2]

# 7. Smaller Project with High Plot Size
small_high_plot <- df %>%
  filter(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)` < quantile(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`, 0.25)) %>%
  slice(which.max(`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`, `TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`, `AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)
small_project <- small_high_plot$`PROJECT NAME`
small_total_area <- small_high_plot$`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`
small_avg_area <- small_high_plot$`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`

# 8. Mid-range Balanced Development
mid_range <- df %>%
  filter(between(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`, quantile(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`, 0.25), quantile(`TOTAL LAND AREA (sqm)`, 0.75)),
         between(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`, quantile(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`, 0.25), quantile(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`, 0.75))) %>%
  slice(1:2) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`)
mid_project_1 <- mid_range$`PROJECT NAME`[1]
mid_project_2 <- mid_range$`PROJECT NAME`[2 %in% seq_len(nrow(mid_range))] %||% "None"

# 9. Opportunity Zones
opportunity_zones <- df %>%
  filter(`NO OF PLOTS` > median(`NO OF PLOTS`),
         `NO. OF PROPERTIES` > median(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`)) %>%
  arrange(desc(`NO OF PLOTS`)) %>%
  slice(1:3) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`)
opp_zone_1 <- opportunity_zones$`PROJECT NAME`[1]
opp_zone_2 <- opportunity_zones$`PROJECT NAME`[2 %in% seq_len(nrow(opportunity_zones))] %||% "None"
opp_zone_3 <- opportunity_zones$`PROJECT NAME`[3 %in% seq_len(nrow(opportunity_zones))] %||% "None"

# 10. Urban Planning Insight
high_density_zone <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(`NO. OF PROPERTIES`)) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`)
high_density_project <- high_density_zone$`PROJECT NAME`
low_density_1 <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(1) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`)
low_density_project_1 <- low_density_1$`PROJECT NAME`
low_density_2 <- df %>%
  arrange(desc(`AVG. LAND AREA (sqm)`)) %>%
  slice(2) %>%
  select(`PROJECT NAME`)
low_density_project_2 <- low_density_2$`PROJECT NAME`

# Display the datatable
datatable(df)
```

# Graph

```{r,warning=FALSE}

df <- read.csv("~/7.Narration/0.Consolidate/Input/4.Graph/graph data.csv")


# 1. Peak supply year
peak_supply <- df %>%
  slice(which.max(supply)) %>%
  select(year, supply)
peak_year <- peak_supply$year
peak_value <- peak_supply$supply


# 2. Lowest supply year
low_supply <- df %>%
  slice(which.min(supply)) %>%
  select(year, supply)
low_year <- low_supply$year
low_value <- low_supply$supply

# 3. Average supply over 5 years
avg_supply <- mean(df$supply)

# 4. Drop in supply from Peak to Present
drop_from_peak <- peak_value - df$supply[df$year == 2025]

# 5. Stable Period (2021–2023)
stable_year <- df %>%
  filter(year %in% c(2021, 2022, 2023))

# Display table
datatable(df)
```
